added_lemmas.justification: The theorem establishes a sharp generic calibration elbow: no cross-view pair leaves at least two structural coefficient tuples, whereas any one preassigned pair identifies the common order and the complete full-view coefficient tuple, simultaneously for all pairs off one explicit algebraic locus.
added_lemmas.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and Theorem 3 obtain full-pair identification using edgewise cross-view correlation diversity. On the narrower component-aligned Gaussian class, this theorem imposes neither that diversity condition nor edge minimality, proves that every pair works simultaneously outside one proper algebraic set, and supplies the matching marginal-only lower bound. This is a different observation-regime result, not a containment claim for their published class.
added_lemmas.consumer: A coordinate-aligned repeated-sensor study may calibrate any two participants or views jointly for order recovery, retain every other view only through its marginal covariance for coefficient recovery, and know that zero paired blocks cannot generically identify the tuple.

proposed.name: \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\)
proposed.construction: For fixed \(p\ge2\), \(m\ge2\), and \(\pi_0\in\mathfrak S_V\), define \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}=\{\theta=((B^{(a)})_{a\in M},(\Gamma_i)_{i\in V}):B^{(a)}[\pi_0(k),\pi_0(j)]=0\text{ whenever }j\ge k,\ \Gamma_i\in\mathbb S_{++}^{m}\text{ for every }a\in M,i\in V\}\). Give this set the relative Euclidean topology on the free strictly \(\pi_0\)-lower-triangular coefficients and symmetric covariance entries. Each \(\theta\) induces \(\Sigma_\theta^{ab}=(I_p-B^{(a)})^{-1}\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i[a,b])(I_p-B^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}\), hence a centered component-aligned Gaussian law.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The original lower bound \(m\ge3\) is not used by the fixed-order parameterization, its positive-definite covariance formula, or the pairwise inversion witness. Replacing it by the sharp \(m\ge2\) domain is necessary to state the calibration elbow for the two-view case; \(m\ge3\) is required only when calling a calibrated pair a proper subset of all views.

The active directive strengthens the headline from a fixed-pair sufficiency theorem under the convention that at least two views are admissible to a simultaneous all-pairs theorem with a matching marginal-only lower bound. Because claim changes cannot be broadened through a narrowing proposal, the stronger proved theorem replaces the obsolete narrower node and receives its inbound dependencies.

prose_updates.tldr: On the restrictive component-aligned Gaussian LiMVAM class, there is a sharp generic calibration elbow. A single algebraic exceptional set \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\) is proper and relatively null; outside it, every preassigned view pair simultaneously identifies the common order and every view-specific coefficient matrix, while all viewwise marginals with no paired cross-block leave at least two distinct coefficient tuples. Thus zero paired blocks are generically insufficient, any one paired block is sufficient, and the minimum number of jointly calibrated views is exactly two even when zero- and one-view designs are admitted. For each fixed pair, its algebraic exceptional set is exactly the order-nonidentification locus, whereas coefficient nonidentification can be strictly smaller because different orders may produce the same tuple. The result uses no edge minimality or Heurtebise et al. diversity assumption, but it is for a narrower disturbance class; removed-set recursion, uncertainty-aware inversion, and the still-open exact-once quotient enumeration remain separate supporting components.

project_justification.gap: Heurtebise et al.'s Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and Theorem 3 give full-pair identification under edgewise correlation diversity on their broader disturbance class. Existing recursive LiNGAM results explain how to remove a true exogenous variable but do not give the complete partial-calibration frontier here. None of these results proves both halves of the sharp observation elbow on the component-aligned Gaussian class: that every single preassigned pair works simultaneously off one explicit proper algebraic set, and that all marginals without any cross-view block generically fail to identify the coefficient tuple.
project_justification.niche: On the component-aligned subclass, each proposed order uniquely determines all view-specific coefficients from marginal modified Cholesky regressions. Paired cross-covariance blocks are needed only to test the observable diagonal residual restrictions that discriminate orders. This separation makes it possible to prove both a no-pair lower bound and a one-pair upper bound without discarding marginal information from any view.
project_justification.fill: The replacement headline multiplies the denominator-cleared wrong-order residual polynomials over every unordered view pair and every wrong order, proves the product nonzero using explicit pairwise inversion witnesses, and obtains simultaneous pairwise point identification outside its null zero locus. It also constructs, for every order, a positive-definite diagonal cross-view noise completion matching all marginals, proves every order marginally compatible, and shows that outside the all-pairs exceptional set at least two numerical coefficient tuples survive. Fixed-pair failure is characterized exactly for order identification, with a zero-edge witness proving that duplicate orders can make the coefficient-failure locus strictly smaller.

prose_updates.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the flagship model anchor. Its Section 4.6, Assumption 2 requires edgewise cross-view correlation diversity, and its Theorem 3 identifies the causal partial order and view-specific coefficient matrices from full pairing, with an additional assumption used for a unique total order. On the intersection of those assumptions with the narrower component-aligned Gaussian subclass, its full-pair singleton agrees with \(\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\); this is only a restricted-domain consistency comparison. The new headline concerns a different observation regime and does not claim containment of their published class: on the narrower class, one algebraic set \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\) controls all pairs simultaneously, any one preassigned pair identifies off that set without edge minimality or their diversity assumption, and no paired block leaves multiple coefficient tuples generically. The exact fixed-pair order-failure locus and the possible strict reduction caused by duplicate numerical tuples refine that comparison. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM, Section 3.1, Lemmas 1--2 and Corollary 1, supports the recursive-residual comparison but does not prove removed-set path independence or enumerate all compatible orders. Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM, ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausal, and GhassamiEtAl2018MultiDomain share information across groups or domains through non-Gaussianity, population components, or domain heterogeneity rather than selected paired covariance blocks. HyttinenEberhardtHoyer2012Overlapping studies concerns experimental total effects, not paired-view residual covariance restrictions. The enumeration, hitting-set, covariance-concentration, and set-inversion references continue to support their respective computational and finite-sample components; none supplies the sharp no-pair/one-pair population elbow proved here. TaylorEtAl2017CamCAN remains a future diagnostic use case and does not validate component alignment or calibration sampling.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The simultaneous generic theorem is relative to the finite-dimensional fixed-order component-aligned parameterization and supplies no uniform distance from \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\). Near this algebraic set, finite-sample order recovery can be unstable. Each \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\) exactly marks order nonidentification for its pair, but numerical coefficient duplication means it can overstate coefficient nonidentification; the zero-edge identity-noise point is an explicit example. The marginal-only lower bound is a population statement and depends on allowing positive-definite diagonal cross-view noise completions. The \(2^p\)-state result counts exact-real arithmetic operations and does not establish polynomial bit complexity, and exact-once quotient output remains confined to \(\text{oeq:output-sensitive-quotient}\). At population moments a positive model-distance diagnostic falsifies the maintained class on observed calibration blocks, but finite-sample non-rejection does not validate the class or unobserved pairs.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The generic all-pairs exceptional-set theorem, the exact no-pair/one-pair elbow, fixed-order completion, removed-set recursion, essential poset, local stability analysis, and covariance-region inversion are obligations only on the component-aligned Gaussian subclass. Genericity is relative to coefficients respecting a fixed \(\pi_0\) and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. It supplies neither a uniform identification margin nor point identification on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\). Joint Gaussianity and component alignment exclude broader LiMVAM disturbance models, positive-definite \(\Gamma_i\) excludes singular shared-noise limits, and the repeated-sensor interpretation applies only to coordinate-aligned measurements. The comparison with Heurtebise et al. is restricted to the intersection with their assumptions and is not a claim that the present class contains theirs. Calibration-plus-marginals sampling, selection, and transport restrictions remain as previously stated; Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI remain future diagnostic applications. Output-sensitive quotient enumeration remains open.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives the sharp generic calibration frontier: the absence of every paired cross-block prevents identification of the structural tuple, while any single preassigned pair identifies it, simultaneously across all pair choices outside one explicit proper algebraic set.
statement_notes.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM obtains full-pair identification under edgewise diversity on a broader disturbance class. The present result is for a narrower component-aligned Gaussian class, removes that diversity requirement within this class, changes the observation regime to one arbitrary pair, and adds the matching marginal-only impossibility result; it is not a class-containment claim.
statement_notes.consumer: A coordinate-aligned study can certify that exactly two jointly calibrated views are generically necessary and sufficient for order and full-tuple recovery, while using every other view marginally for its coefficients.
